Contract or expected behavior: Protected student data: components.schemas.StudentRequest.properties.dateOfBirth is marked writeOnly: true and states 'it is accepted on write and is never returned by the API.' StudentResponse omits dateOfBirth.
Actual behavior: GET /api/students/{id} and GET /api/students return the dateOfBirth property in the JSON payload (e.g., "dateOfBirth": "2004-01-06" in Scenario 12 Step 2, or null when unset).

Contract or expected behavior: POST /api/students description promises: 'Creates a student and places them on the roster of any courses listed in courses.' PUT /api/students/{id} description promises: 'Replaces the student's details and, when courses is supplied, their course enrollments.'
Actual behavior: Both POST and PUT silently ignore the courses array in StudentRequest. The student is created/updated, but the target courses' rosters and enrollment counts remain 0 (Scenario 01 Step 3, Scenario 03 Step 6).
Steps to reproduce: 1. POST /api/courses (creates course 45) -> 2. POST /api/students with "courses": [45] -> 3. GET /api/courses/getEnrollment/45 (returns 0) and GET /api/courses/45 (roster is []). Same occurs on PUT /api/students/83 with "courses": [48].

Contract or expected behavior: Operation description promises 200 OK with an array of CourseResponse objects ('Returns the full details of each course the student is enrolled in').
Actual behavior: Returns 501 Not Implemented with body {"status":501,"error":"Not Implemented","message":"Not implemented yet","path":"/api/students/82/courses"} (Scenario 02 Step 5).
Steps to reproduce: 1. POST /api/courses (id 46) -> 2. POST /api/students (id 82) -> 3. PUT /api/courses/addStudent/46 with body 82 -> 4. GET /api/students/82/courses

Contract or expected behavior: Accepts RosterChangeRequest ({"studentId": <id>}) and returns 200 OK with updated CourseResponse when removing an enrolled student, or 409 Conflict when the student is not on the roster.
Actual behavior: Always fails with 400 Bad Request regardless of whether the student is enrolled on the roster (Scenario 02 Step 6) or not on the roster (Scenario 09 Step 3).
Steps to reproduce: 1. POST /api/courses (id 46) -> 2. POST /api/students (id 82) -> 3. PUT /api/courses/addStudent/46 with body 82 -> 4. PUT /api/courses/removeStudent/46 with body {"studentId": 82}

Contract or expected behavior: Responses section promises 200 OK with Content-Type application/json matching CourseResponse ('The course with its updated roster').
Actual behavior: Returns 200 OK with Content-Type text/plain;charset=UTF-8 and plain text body '<Name> added successfully', causing JSON parsers in clients to crash with SyntaxError/JSONError (Scenario 02 Step 3, Scenario 05 Steps 5-6).

Contract or expected behavior: POST /api/students promises 201 Created with Location header and StudentResponse JSON body. PUT /api/students/{id} promises 200 OK with StudentResponse JSON body (id, name, major, gpa, courses).
Actual behavior: POST returns 200 OK (missing Location header) with {"id": <id>, "message": "<Name> added successfully"}. PUT returns 200 OK with {"message": "<Name> updated successfully"}, omitting required StudentResponse fields (Scenarios 01, 03, 04, 06, 12).
Steps to reproduce: 1. POST /api/students with valid StudentRequest -> 2. PUT /api/students/83 with valid StudentRequest

Type: Contract drift (Schema structural mismatch & enum violation)
Contract or expected behavior: CourseResponse requires property 'instructorId' (integer), 'roster' as an array of StudentSummary objects ({id, name}), and 'status' enum restricted to ['OPEN', 'CLOSED'].
Actual behavior: Returns 'instructor' instead of 'instructorId', returns 'roster' as an array of plain student name strings (e.g., ["Preserved Student"]) instead of StudentSummary objects, and returns undocumented status 'FULL' instead of 'CLOSED' when at capacity (Scenario 07 Step 4, Scenario 13 Step 3).
Steps to reproduce: 1. POST /api/students (id 92, 93) -> 2. POST /api/courses with maxSize 5 and roster [92, 93] -> 3. PUT /api/courses/50 with maxSize 2

Type: Integration fault (Unhandled server exception on capacity limit)
Contract or expected behavior: PUT /api/courses/addStudent/{courseId} promises 409 Conflict when the course is full. PUT /api/courses/{id} promises 400 Bad Request when maxSize is set below the current roster size.
Actual behavior: Both operations fail with an unhandled 500 Internal Server Error ('An unexpected error occurred') when capacity constraints are violated (Scenario 05 Step 7, Scenario 07 Step 5).
Steps to reproduce: 1. POST /api/courses with maxSize 2 (id 49) -> 2. Add 2 students via PUT /api/courses/addStudent/49 -> 3. Add 3rd student via PUT /api/courses/addStudent/49 (returns 500). Or PUT /api/courses/50 with maxSize 1 when 2 students are on the roster (returns 500).

Type: Integration fault (Missing state & referential integrity checks)
Contract or expected behavior: PUT /api/courses/addStudent/{courseId} promises 409 Conflict if the student is already on the roster. POST /api/courses promises 404 Not Found if initial roster contains a non-existent student ID.
Actual behavior: PUT /api/courses/addStudent/{courseId} returns 200 OK on duplicate enrollment (Scenario 08 Step 4). POST /api/courses with unknown student ID [999999] returns 201 Created and silently drops the invalid ID to produce an empty roster [] (Scenario 10 Step 1).
Steps to reproduce: 1. PUT /api/courses/addStudent/51 with body 94 twice in a row (both return 200). 2. POST /api/courses with body {"name":"Ghost Roster Course","maxSize":10,"room":"Rm 10","roster":[999999]} (returns 201).

Type: Integration fault (Missing boundary validation & error schema drift)
Contract or expected behavior: StudentRequest.properties.name specifies maxLength: 100 and promises 400 Bad Request using the ErrorResponse schema (timestamp, status, error, message, path) when validation fails.
Actual behavior: Accepts a 101-character name with 200 OK (Scenario 06 Step 4). Additionally, when validation does fail (e.g., negative GPA or missing major in Scenarios 04, 06, 11), the 400 response body is a flat map (e.g., {"gpa":"No negative GPAs allowed"}) instead of ErrorResponse.
Steps to reproduce: 1. POST /api/students with a 101-character name string (returns 200 OK). 2. POST /api/students with gpa -0.01 (returns 400 with non-standard error schema).

Contract or expected behavior: DELETE /api/students/{id} promises 204 No Content ('The student was deleted').
Actual behavior: Deletes the student and returns an empty body with 200 OK instead of 204 No Content (Scenario 01 Step 4).
